section_summary: This section records the sinking of the Akashi Maru No. 105 and other seizures of Japanese fishing vessels, alongside Japanese requests for protests and discussion of a United States naval patrol. It also covers changes and proposed changes to Japan’s authorized fishing area, Far Eastern Commission negotiations, a dispute over Army fish purchases, and reports on lactating whales taken during the 1948–49 Antarctic season. The section ends mid-document, in a draft memorandum supporting a northern extension of the fishing area.

subfiles.title: Akashi Maru casualty list
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Lists dead, missing and surviving crew from the Akashi Maru No. 105.
subfiles.summary: Final page of an earlier enclosure listing casualties and survivors.

subfiles.title: Note to Chinese Mission concerning Akashi Maru
subfiles.about: Requests Chinese information and views on the reported seizure and sinking.
subfiles.summary: Reports the attack and asks that China investigate it.

subfiles.title: Proposed Northern Extension of the Japanese Fishing Area
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks Department views on extending the fishing area around Hokkaido and the southern Kurils.
subfiles.summary: Sebald describes a proposed boundary through Soya and Etorofu Straits, the fishing and navigation problems under the existing line, and the complication posed by SCAPIN 1033’s twelve-mile restriction. He argues that action would also prevent the present fishing line from gaining weight as a future political boundary.

subfiles.title: Sketch of proposed northern fishing area extension
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Illustrates the boundary proposed in despatch no. 594.
subfiles.summary: Map enclosure marking the proposed northern extension.

subfiles.title: Jurich letter forwarding protest
subfiles.about: Forwards a letter opposing a change in Army fish purchasing.
subfiles.summary: Jurich asks Chapman to assist with the issue raised with Senator Magnuson.

subfiles.title: Protest over Army fish purchases for occupation troops
subfiles.about: Protests the Army’s reported plan to stop buying Seattle fish for troops in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Jurich says the change threatens fishing employment in the Pacific Northwest.

subfiles.title: Reply to Jurich on Army fish procurement
subfiles.about: Explains the Army directive favoring local purchases for occupation forces in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Looney says Japan accounted for about one-fifth of recent Army fish purchases from Seattle and San Francisco. The Seattle center will continue supplying other areas, and his office sees no appropriate action to take.

subfiles.title: Sinking of Japanese Fishing Vessel by Chinese Patrol
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese reports and a request for protest over the Akashi Maru sinking and other seizures.
subfiles.summary: Sebald summarizes evidence placing the Akashi Maru within the authorized fishing area and forwards reports of other Chinese seizures and a broader detention table. He notes that the Diplomatic Section had already raised the sinking with the Chinese Mission.

subfiles.title: Japanese request for protest over Akashi Maru
subfiles.from: Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs; signed Ichiro Ohta
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Asks SCAP to protest the sinking and seek measures against further attacks.
subfiles.summary: The ministry recounts the attack, argues that it violated international law regardless of the waters’ status, and asks SCAP to protest to China.

subfiles.title: Report on No. 105 Akashi Maru
subfiles.from: T. Okubo, Director-General, Maritime Safety Board
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Documents the Akashi Maru’s capture, shelling, casualties and rescue.
subfiles.summary: The report gives estimated positions within the MacArthur Line, describes pursuit and forced towing by an unidentified warship, and recounts gunfire that sank the fishing boat. It names four dead and four missing crew members and describes the rescue and eventual return of four survivors.

subfiles.title: Reports on vessels seized by Chinese
subfiles.about: Records seizures of the Miho Maru, Tokai Maru, Kasho Maru No. 5 and two Zenshin Maru vessels.
subfiles.summary: The report describes the May seizure and escape of the Miho Maru, with the Tokai Maru left detained. Crew accounts then describe the June capture of the Kasho Maru No. 5 and Zenshin Maru Nos. 3 and 5, confiscation of documents and belongings, the detention of several crew members, and the return of others aboard Zenshin Maru No. 3.

subfiles.title: Information on Ships Detained
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates Japanese vessels detained in connection with Korea, Soviet forces and China.
subfiles.summary: The table records vessel names, owners, locations, detention dates, and whether ships and crews returned. It includes the Chinese seizures discussed elsewhere in the despatch as well as numerous Korean and Soviet cases.

subfiles.title: Japanese fishing—FEC
subfiles.to: W. M. Chapman, Flory and Barnett
subfiles.about: Records discussions with Koo about scheduling the FEC fisheries subcommittee.
subfiles.summary: Castleman and Koo agree to wait for United States instructions before meeting again.

subfiles.title: Inter-Agency Meeting re FEC Fishing Paper
subfiles.about: Records interagency decisions on the United States position in FEC fishing negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Participants agree to keep the substance of existing instructions and avoid giving Canada assurances about a 150-mile coastal exclusion. They consider Australian wording, a Chinese objection to the fishing boundary, and a Soviet inquiry about recent expansion.

subfiles.title: Enlargement of Authorized Japanese Fishing Area
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports SCAPIN 2046’s eastern extension and reduction of the island clearance limit.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports that SCAPIN 2046 extends the authorized area eastward and reduces the required distance from non-Japanese administered land from twelve to three miles. He gives projected catches, notes favorable Japanese reaction, and forwards the directive and a newspaper editorial.

subfiles.title: Area Authorized for Japanese Fishing and Whaling
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Rescinds earlier fishing-area memoranda and sets new boundaries and conditions.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 2046 specifies the authorized fishing and whaling boundary, a three-mile restriction around land outside Japanese administration, and limits on landing or contact. It states that the authorization settles no future jurisdiction, boundary or fishing-rights question.

subfiles.title: Expansion of Fishing Grounds
subfiles.about: Welcomes the fishing-area expansion while urging compliance and conservation.
subfiles.summary: The editorial links further access to curbing poaching and overfishing.

subfiles.title: United States Naval Patrol in East China Sea
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports plans for naval patrols to prevent seizures of Japanese fishing boats.
subfiles.summary: Sebald recounts his Mission’s objections to a regular patrol because of possible political consequences, and describes SCAP’s competing request for naval help. He reports that a ten-day Seventh Task Fleet patrol had been ordered, with force authorized to protect Japanese vessels.

subfiles.title: Proposed Radio to DA Concerning Naval Patrol in East China Sea
subfiles.about: Presents staff positions on requesting Seventh Task Fleet patrol assistance.
subfiles.summary: The sheet summarizes earlier messages, Diplomatic Section objections, and G-3’s preference for routine sweeps. The Natural Resources Section recommends requesting a regular patrol.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese lactating-whale report
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, London
subfiles.about: Requests forwarding of a Japanese whaling report to the International Whaling Commission.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the report for transmission if no objection is perceived.

subfiles.title: Report on Lactating Whales Taken by 1948–49 Antarctic Whaling Operation
subfiles.from: Japanese Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Reports the investigation of three lactating whales killed during Antarctic whaling.
subfiles.summary: Prosecutors dismissed the cases for insufficient evidence that calves accompanied the whales.

subfiles.title: Army request to forward whaling report
subfiles.from: Acting Chief, Far Eastern Affairs Group, Department of the Army
subfiles.to: J. R. Kennedy, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of the Japanese whaling report to the International Whaling Commission.
subfiles.summary: The Army forwards report copies and asks that one reach the Commission.

subfiles.title: Violation Cases of the International Whaling Regulations
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Details three suspected cases involving lactating fin and blue whales.
subfiles.summary: Lists vessels, gunners, dates, whale measurements and anatomical observations, and records withheld bonuses and referral of the gunners for investigation.

subfiles.title: Summary of FEC steering and commission meetings
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports proposed amendments to the FEC fishing and aquatic industries paper.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes British and Chinese amendments and delegates’ responses.

subfiles.title: Plan to Use US Navy to Enforce Japanese Fishing Area
subfiles.to: Secretary and Under Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Alerts senior officials to a planned naval patrol and its diplomatic risks.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum says the Department was not consulted on the patrol plan.

subfiles.title: Reply to Soviet inquiry on Japanese fisheries conservation
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Suggests a response on the status of SCAP’s fisheries conservation report.
subfiles.summary: A detailed report is expected in February 1950; interim inquiries may go to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Proposed Northern Extension of the Japanese Fishing Area
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Requests prompt Department views on a northern boundary proposal initiated by SCAP’s Natural Resources Section.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards draft materials and argues that a proposal would show SCAP did not regard the existing line near Hokkaido as permanent. He asks for the Department’s position before the proposal advances.

subfiles.title: Extension of the Northern Boundary of Authorized Fishing Area
subfiles.about: Seeks comment on a proposed northern extension and draft letter to the Soviet representative.
subfiles.summary: The section cites fishing losses, stalled Far Eastern Commission deliberations and the risk that the current line could influence peace settlement boundaries. It asks the Diplomatic Section to comment on drafts.

subfiles.title: Draft memorandum on northern fishing boundary
subfiles.about: Sets out the case for changing the authorized boundary north and northeast of Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: Opening page cites lost production, fishermen’s hardship and navigation hazards; the draft continues beyond this section.
